strengths: Addresses a well-motivated, practically relevant problem in LLM alignment: the diversity-quality tradeoff
Comprehensive and rigorous evaluation across 13 metrics (11 diversity × 2 quality), multiple datasets, model families, and both automatic and human evaluation

Thoughtful evaluation design: separates lexical vs. semantic diversity, extends to discourse-level diversity for long-form generation, uses Coverage/Dominance metrics from multi-objective optimization
Practical, deployable approach requiring only inference-time modifications with no retraining
Consistent empirical results across datasets with 21.3% best-case joint improvement
Strong experimental methodology including ablation studies (random routing, aligned-aligned collaboration, -JUDGE) and contribution analysis
Well-presented with clear motivation, effective visualizations, and honest discussion of failure modes and limitations
Extensive supplementary materials with implementation details and annotation protocols support reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: model combination and weighted routing are well-established; relies heavily on Fei et al. (2025)'s superficial alignment hypothesis; routing strategies are simple heuristics

Unresolved critical failure mode: Section 6.2 identifies inherent early stopping when routing to base model that can truncate outputs; proposed 'restart sampling' solution is unsatisfying and adds complexity

Router design lacks principled foundation: multiple ad-hoc strategies without systematic design methodology; no clear guidance for selecting routers on new domains; hyperparameter γ requires tuning with unclear selection methodology
Methodological concern: human evaluation uses 'matched quality' comparison which may artificially favor BACO and mask scenarios where it struggles
Shallow theoretical understanding: why these specific heuristics work is not explained beyond superficial alignment hypothesis
Incomplete comparisons: missing recent diversity-promotion methods (2024-2025); NUDGING comparison limited to quality; ensemble baselines are relatively weak
Evaluation scale limitations: only 10 samples per prompt; moderate inter-rater agreement on diversity (κ=0.166-0.244); human evaluation on only 20 prompts per dataset
Computational cost not substantiated: runtime overhead of dual-model inference not reported; efficiency claims based on superficial alignment not empirically validated
Limited scope and generalization: only 2 model families tested; requires availability of both base and aligned versions; unclear performance with significant model divergence
Missing key analyses: frequency/severity of early stopping, statistical significance testing, sensitivity to alignment quality, detailed failure mode investigation
